Foreign Ministry coordinates repatriation of remains of two Sri Lankan workers killed in South Korea

cards.what_happened: Two Sri Lankan migrant workers died in a road accident in Hwaseong, South Korea, at around 9 p.m. on Nov. 26, 2026. The Sri Lankan Embassy in Seoul was informed by Korean police on Nov. 27. Sri Lanka’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism is coordinating with South Korean authorities and the families to repatriate the remains, Acting Minister Arun Hemachandra said.
details: Acting Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism is working with South Korean authorities and the families of the two Sri Lankan migrant workers. The aim is to facilitate the return of their remains after the road accident in Hwaseong, South Korea.
The accident happened at around 9 p.m. on Nov. 26, 2026. The Sri Lankan Embassy in Seoul was officially told by Korean police on Nov. 27.

The Embassy’s Consular Section is coordinating the required formalities with relevant authorities, the ministry and the families. It is doing this to speed up the repatriation process and to give consular and welfare assistance.
Hemachandra said both workers had gone to South Korea after registering with the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE).
key_facts: Two Sri Lankan migrant workers died in a road accident in Hwaseong, South Korea.
The accident occurred at around 9 p.m. on Nov. 26, 2026.
Korean police officially informed the Sri Lankan Embassy in Seoul on Nov. 27.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism is coordinating repatriation.
It is working with South Korean authorities and the families of the two workers.
The Embassy’s Consular Section is coordinating formalities to expedite repatriation and provide consular and welfare assistance.
Acting Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra gave the information.
Both workers had registered with the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE) before going to South Korea.

cards.blurb: Sri Lanka is working with South Korea and families to bring home the remains of two workers killed in a Hwaseong road accident.
cards.spoken: Two Sri Lankan migrant workers have died in a road accident in Hwaseong, South Korea. The crash happened at around nine p.m. on November twenty-sixth, twenty twenty-six, and Korean police officially informed the Sri Lankan Embassy in Seoul the next day, on November twenty-seventh. Acting Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra says the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism is now working with South Korean authorities and the families to bring the remains back. The Embassy’s Consular Section is handling the required formalities with the relevant authorities, the ministry and the families. It is trying to speed up the repatriation and provide consular and welfare assistance. Hemachandra also said both workers had travelled to South Korea after registering with the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment.
